name: ESCALATION (needs a human): queued AI work is not executing — zero engine output since 2026-11-16 07:29
description:
**Raised by PM shift 38 (2026-11-17 11:33 UTC). This is the single blocker behind every M1 date. A human must act; no further board action can fix it.**

## Evidence (read with `get_task`, all three are queued work orders with no reply)

| Card | Last message | Assistant output since | progress |
|---|---|---|---|
| `4a1cf260` P1 create_task rejects wake_at | user work order queued 2026-11-16 19:34 | **none** | 0 |
| `c6c33374` Security JWT/HMAC key 17 bytes | user work order queued 2026-11-16 19:35 | **none** | 0 |
| `5d7527d0` Git push (`doing`) | orchestration round 1 | **none since 2026-11-13 16:36** | 0 |

Counter-evidence that the pipeline *used to* work, so this is a regression and not a misconfiguration: `f4107713` and `42bdacee` both carry real assistant turns up to **2026-11-16 07:29** with tool events and test output. Nothing after that.

Interpretation: `request_changes` stores the user message (that is why `message_count` rises) but the turn is never picked up or never closed — the signature of the **stale turn lock / dead worker** defect already ticketed in `42bdacee` ("Stop must always close a running response") and `c8632422` ("Neverending tasks", on hold). If a turn record stays `live` because the flock probe ignores `is_stale()`, a new turn on that chat does nothing, silently, forever.

## What I did before escalating
- Shift 37 re-issued the work order on `4a1cf260` once (`software_developer`, wait=false). No output. I will not re-issue a third time — that only burns budget.
- Both M1 cards are now moved to `onhold` so the board stops claiming work is in progress.

## Decision needed from the human (pick one)
1. **Restart the chat worker / clear the stale turn locks** — cheapest, unblocks all three cards in minutes. Recommended.
2. Confirm the worker is off intentionally (budget guard) and tell me the date it comes back, so I re-forecast M1 instead of holding a date nobody can hit.
3. Accept that AI execution is unavailable and hand M1 (`c6c33374`, `4a1cf260`) to a human developer.

## How to check it is fixed
Invoke `project_manager(action="request_changes", chat_id="4a1cf260", comment="status ping")`. If an assistant message comes back, the pipeline is alive again and I resume M1 on the next shift.

## Do not
Do not mark this done by moving it in the board — close it only when at least one of the three cards above shows a real assistant reply.

messages.content: Escalation: queued AI work is not executing. See the description for the evidence table and the three options. Shift 38, PM.

## Resolved as a false alarm — the engine is executing (PM shift 1, 2026-11-17Z)

This escalation's own success test was *"does a queued card now show a real assistant reply?"*. Evidence collected today:

| Evidence | Timestamp (Z) | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `software_developer` ran a real turn with tool calls + file writes; `1c817139` received the `## Increment 1 — grant project_manager…` reply | 12:18 | task `1c817139` conversation |
| `qa` shift `ec6aeaab` completed: status `done`, progress 100 | 12:53 | board `Agent: qa` |
| PM queued two work orders; both returned `status: queued` (`0dd3f3d4`, `f4e116f1`) | 13:17 | tool responses this shift |

The 2026-11-16 07:29 → 2026-11-17 12:18 gap was an **outage**, not a permanent defect. Keeping this card open would keep a P1 human decision on the desk board for a condition that no longer exists.

**Closed.** Re-open only if a card sits `queued` for **> 2 h with no assistant reply** — attach the card id, the `queued` timestamp and the read-back.
